general.temas: The November 29 general election dominates the front pages, particularly the four-way debate, the parties’ proposals and tactical voting. The appointment of Hernández de Cos to the ECB, Spain’s qualification for the Davis Cup semi-finals and RTVE’s backing for Silvia Intxaurrondo also feature repeatedly. Only El Mundo highlights the sinking of a ship off Ibiza.
general.motivo_crispacion: The election campaign accounts for much of the tension, with a debate between candidates and headlines reflecting criticism between parties and political blocs. Público reports allegations of property speculation and a supposed judicial war, while OKdiario reports that Sánchez was insulted as he arrived at the debate. Electoral proceedings against Intxaurrondo and Ayuso are also causing controversy, as are investigations into possible irregularities in Navarre. Sports, culture and health stories provide a less contentious counterpoint.

El País.resumen:
- The front page focuses on the November 29 election, with a comparison of party manifestos and interviews with the candidates.
- The four-way debate brings together Sánchez, Feijóo, Abascal and Colau.
- Polls examine tactical voting, seats where the outcome is undecided and possible majorities.
- A judge circulates a video against the government and Silvia Intxaurrondo; RTVE backs the journalist amid electoral proceedings against her.
- The front page reports remarks by José Bono, Vox’s proposed cuts and electoral proceedings opened against Ayuso.
El País.motivo_populismo: An informative tone predominates, although expressions such as “Milei’s chainsaw”, “key debate” and “against the government” add drama and a confrontational angle.
El País.sesgo: The selection prioritizes the campaign and competition between political blocs, and pays critical attention to the actions of Vox, Ayuso and a judge opposed to the government. It also highlights RTVE’s support for Silvia Intxaurrondo; this reflects an editorial approach, though it is not enough on its own to establish a political affiliation.

El Mundo.resumen:
- The front page offers an election questionnaire and examines how four candidates connect with voters.
- Hernández de Cos will be the next president of the ECB, according to the published report.
- Possible irregularities in a construction project in Navarre and the reduction of Judge Biedma’s security detail are highlighted.
- It reports the sinking of a ship near Ibiza, with no spill according to the authorities, and details its cargo and route.
- Also featured are the rise in lung cancer among women, Russian casualties in Ukraine and Spain’s qualification for the Davis Cup semi-finals.
El Mundo.motivo_populismo: Most headlines are informative, but expressions such as “the sewers of Ferraz”, “Putin’s meat grinder” and “mountain of dead” resort to disparagement or emotionally intense imagery.
El Mundo.sesgo: The selection gives prominent space to politics and judicial matters affecting leaders or circles linked to the PSOE. The expression “the sewers of Ferraz” introduces an accusatory angle, while other stories use more descriptive wording.

ABC.resumen:
- Coverage of the election debate between Sánchez, Colau, Feijóo and Abascal.
- The Interior Ministry has provided special protection to the head of Morocco’s intelligence services since 2022.
- The RTVE board backs Silvia Intxaurrondo after the Central Electoral Board opened proceedings against her.
- The front page covers the personal lives of several candidates and housing proposals.
- It also includes sports news, the Mad Cool festival and the National Lottery.
ABC.motivo_populismo: An informative tone predominates, although expressions such as “spy chief”, “rushes to defend” and “regains its pride” add drama or emotional weight.
ABC.sesgo: The selection gives considerable weight to the election campaign and combines political reporting with personal details about the candidates. Some headlines present institutional decisions with a critical or dramatized slant, but no unambiguous ideological orientation is apparent.

Público.resumen:
- Ada Colau criticizes property investment funds, the PSOE and economic powers.
- Podemos intensifies its campaign and questions its exclusion from the debates.
- Several pieces cover the election debate, tactical voting and the Broad Front.
- The front page criticizes Feijóo’s record and the PP in Andalusia.
- It also reports Hernández de Cos’s appointment and a tribute to women.
Público.motivo_populismo: Expressions such as “vulture funds”, “judicial war” and “cold feet”, along with “the truth about his record”, use confrontational and sensationalist language.
Público.sesgo: The selection and wording show an approach favorable to left-wing groups such as Podemos and the Broad Front, with criticism of the PP, the PSOE and economic powers.

OKdiario.resumen:
- The front page follows the four-way election debate and highlights gestures and protests surrounding it.
- Residents abroad account for 20% of new voters in the November 29 election.
- Spain reaches the Davis Cup semi-finals; Ferrer hopes to have Alcaraz available.
- Football features in several stories, including the Under-21 draw and Getafe and Celta’s results.
- Also featured are an interview with Raphael and the story of a woman who lives alone in an Asturian village.
OKdiario.motivo_populismo: An informative tone predominates, although some headlines emphasize conflict and emotion with expressions such as “traitor!”, “battle” and “heroic feat”.
OKdiario.sesgo: The selection gives ample space to the election and sport, and its political coverage highlights gestures, protests and clothing as well as the debate. No clear partisan preference is apparent from these headlines.

opiniones.comunista:
As the election debate approaches, I do not want to judge politics by how smoothly the candidates speak, but by the class interests they defend. Vox’s proposal to cut public spending by €112 billion raises a basic question: who would pay the price? When public services are weakened, working people lose rights and become more exposed to private profiteering.

The housing crisis also shows that leaving a basic need to speculation does not guarantee affordable homes. I support expanding public housing and collective ownership, with democratic management, so that having a roof over one’s head does not depend on returns for big capital. Voting matters, but so does the day-to-day organization of the working class: no social right can endure without collective strength to defend it.
opiniones.anarquista:
I see how the election debate and calculations about tactical voting reduce politics to choosing who will govern in our name. I do not look down on those who vote to stop a specific threat, but I distrust the promise that changing leaders is enough to change a structure that concentrates power. Freedom should not be limited to casting a ballot every so often.

Vox’s proposal to cut public spending does not strike me as an emancipatory alternative either: shrinking the state without challenging economic power can leave more people at the mercy of those who own the resources. I support another way forward: organizing housing, care and work from the bottom up, through free associations, mutual aid and decisions made by those affected. Self-management alone does not guarantee equality, but it makes it possible to challenge hierarchies instead of asking their permission.
opiniones.liberal:
As the election debate approaches, I expect less competition over slogans and more answers about how much power and money should remain in citizens’ hands. I support low taxes and a limited state because working, starting a business and saving should expand our freedom, not make us dependent on political decisions.

Vox’s proposal to cut spending deserves rigorous examination: announcing a figure is not enough; it must explain which budget items would be eliminated and how the state’s essential functions would be protected. I also disagree with the idea of making life impossible for property investors. To ease the housing problem, I prefer stable rules and fewer obstacles to construction: driving away capital does not create homes. Economic freedom requires personal responsibility, competition and an accountable government.
opiniones.extrema_derecha:
I hope the election debate serves a purpose beyond trading slogans and calculating political blocs. I want to know who is willing to defend Spain’s sovereignty, strictly control its borders and demand that immigration comply with our laws and our capacity to receive newcomers. The report about Spain’s protection of the head of Morocco’s intelligence services deserves clear explanations: cooperation with Morocco cannot come before national interests.

I also distrust those who promise to manage public money better without tackling waste. The investigation into the Belate tunnel works must establish the facts without privileges or premature convictions.

In contrast to politics turned into a spectacle, I support independent institutions, security and respect for our traditions and families. A polling model should not decide the vote; the conscience of each Spaniard should.
opiniones.centro:
I hope the four-way debate serves a purpose beyond measuring who commands the studio. I want to hear comparable proposals, their costs and the possible alliances needed to carry them out. Polls help us understand the landscape, but they do not replace voters’ judgment or turn a likely majority into a certain result.

I am concerned about Vox’s proposal to cut €112 billion in public spending: before presenting a figure like that as moderate, it must explain which services or benefits would disappear and who would bear the cost. I believe in a dynamic private sector, but also in sustainable social protection. To achieve both, I prefer gradual reforms, rigorous evaluation and broad agreements. And when it comes to electoral proceedings and judicial investigations, I uphold the same principle for everyone: respect for institutions, procedural safeguards and scrutiny without premature convictions.
